content_units: Ontario Fixed-Term Lease Ending on 2026-08-31

This is a   general informational checklist, not legal advice  . For a one-year Ontario residential tenancy running from   2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31  , with   monthly rent   and a plan to leave   at the end of the fixed term  , the key item to verify is whether the tenancy will otherwise continue automatically unless proper notice is given.
End-of-Term Notice Checklist
Item   What to verify   Why it matters   Practical target

Notice timing   Whether tenant must give at least   60 days' written notice   before the end date   In Ontario, fixed-term leases often convert to month-to-month if the tenant stays and no valid termination notice is given   Aim to have notice received by   2026-07-02 or earlier

Termination date   Whether the notice date lines up with the   last day of the rental period / lease term     For monthly tenancies, termination usually must be effective at the end of a rental period   Use   2026-08-31   as the intended termination date

Lease continuation rule   Confirm that the lease does   not need renewal to continue  ; it may roll into month-to-month automatically on same terms, except lawful rent changes   Avoid assuming the tenancy simply ends on its own   Treat notice as still necessary unless official guidance says otherwise

Written records   Keep copy of signed notice, delivery proof, and any landlord acknowledgment   Helps prevent disputes about whether notice was sent on time   Save email/PDF/screenshots and delivery date

Correct form/process   Verify whether using the Ontario tenant notice form/process is recommended or required for your situation   Proper format reduces risk of invalid notice   Check the Landlord and Tenant Board guidance before sending

Move-out condition   Confirm no separate issues exist for keys, cleaning, damage claims, or unpaid amounts   Notice ending the tenancy is separate from property condition/account issues   Plan final clean, key return, and utility/account wrap-up
Lease Renewal and Move-Out Details to Confirm
Lease rollover expectation
- In Ontario, a fixed-term residential lease commonly   does not require signing a new lease   to continue.
- If the tenant remains after   2026-08-31  , the tenancy may continue   month-to-month   under substantially the same terms, subject to lawful changes.
- Because of that, a tenant planning to leave at term end should verify the   notice requirement rather than assume the lease expires automatically  .
Notice details to double-check
- Count back   at least 60 days   from the intended termination date.
- Because the tenancy is   monthly  , confirm the termination date matches the   end of a rental period  .
- If sending by email, only rely on email if the lease or prior consent supports that communication method; otherwise use a delivery method recognized by Ontario tenancy rules.
- If the landlord acknowledges receipt, keep that confirmation.
Documentation to keep
Option 1: Notice packet   Written notice with termination date, tenant names, rental address   Proof of timing
LTB forms
Option 2: Delivery evidence   Email trail, courier confirmation, registered mail receipt, or signed acknowledgment   Proof landlord received it
Service rules
Option 3: Move-out file   Photos/video of unit condition, key return note, utility final bills   Helps with deposit/account questions
Tenant rights
Move-out steps
- Give written notice with   2026-08-31   as the termination date.
- Ask the landlord to confirm receipt in writing.
- Schedule elevator/loading access if the building requires it.
- Take dated photos after cleaning and after removing belongings.
- Return all keys, fobs, garage remotes, and parking/access items.
- Update address for mail, insurance, bank, employer, subscriptions, and government records.
- Confirm utility transfers/cancellations if any accounts are in the tenant's name.
Practical Date Marker for This Scenario
Using the facts provided, a cautious planning date is:
-   Target latest notice receipt date:     2026-07-02
-   Intended move-out / termination date:     2026-08-31
Context used here
- Residential tenancy in   Ontario
-   Rent period:   monthly
- Tenant wants to leave exactly at end of term
- No damage/dispute issue affecting the move-out process
